scenes.title: The map unfolds
scenes.alt: Pip and Milla unfold a paper model map while Dot holds down a curling corner with a smooth stone.
scenes.question: Which detail helps us find our way?
scenes.learningUse: Introduce a picture map; distinguish a model from a real site plan.

scenes.title: A tiny detail
scenes.alt: Dot examines a fallen leaf on a shallow tray with a magnifier beside an open blank notebook.
scenes.question: What can I notice when I slow down?
scenes.learningUse: Observe shape and texture without collecting wild material or naming a species.

scenes.title: Everyone has a viewpoint
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla and Dot join two learners at a low picture stand; a learner using a wheelchair and another wearing glasses point out different details.
scenes.question: What did someone else notice?
scenes.learningUse: Compare observations; provide pointing, speaking, drawing and AAC response routes.

scenes.title: The missing piece
scenes.alt: Milla pauses over an incomplete paper picture model while Dot offers a blank question card.
scenes.question: What do we still need to find out?
scenes.learningUse: Name gaps in a source rather than filling them with guesses.

scenes.title: A quiet listening stop
scenes.alt: Pip rests on a low sage cushion while Dot pauses beside a closed notebook and watches a drifting leaf.
scenes.question: What can we notice without rushing?
scenes.learningUse: Offer a sensory pause, with a quiet indoor alternative and no requirement to close eyes.

scenes.title: The patient seed watch
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla and Dot watch two model seeds and a separate seedling model in a shallow tray; Dot holds an unnumbered calendar card.
scenes.question: What could we check again tomorrow?
scenes.learningUse: Plan repeated observations; distinguish a model from actual germination evidence.

scenes.title: One thing at a time
scenes.alt: Milla and Dot compare two separate faceless potted plant models beside matching tokens and an unlettered comparison card.
scenes.question: What should stay the same?
scenes.learningUse: Introduce fair comparison or, for older learners, controls and possible confounders.

scenes.title: A careful measure
scenes.alt: Pip holds a blank measuring strip beside a separate potted plant; Dot points to the base and Milla records on a blank clipboard.
scenes.question: Where does our measurement start?
scenes.learningUse: Discuss a consistent baseline, method and units; accurate scales are typeset separately.

scenes.title: The surprise result
scenes.alt: Pip and Milla reconsider two blank record cards beside an illustrative plant model with exposed roots.
scenes.question: Does another check change our idea?
scenes.learningUse: Welcome unexpected findings without inventing a growth result or forcing a prediction.

scenes.title: Shade and a water break
scenes.alt: Milla and Dot rest beneath a small sage canopy beside a closed water bottle and two empty cups.
scenes.question: Is it time for a pause?
scenes.learningUse: Normalise rest and hydration; this is not a coffee tasting or advice about plant watering.

scenes.title: The sample station
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla and Dot compare three closed sample containers on a low bench, with stones, bark-like pieces and a plant-texture model.
scenes.question: How can we compare these carefully?
scenes.learningUse: Introduce contained model materials and a repeatable observation routine.

scenes.title: Patterns in a pebble
scenes.alt: Dot uses a magnifier to observe the bands on a large smooth stone in a tray, beside a blank sketch card.
scenes.question: Which feature can I describe?
scenes.learningUse: Use a safe supplied object for texture, pattern and descriptive vocabulary.

scenes.title: The sorting debate
scenes.alt: Pip and Milla consider paper, wood and fabric samples arranged beside two shallow sorting trays.
scenes.question: Could we sort it another way?
scenes.learningUse: Compare justified classification rules; useful for soil models or the Stage 3 paper journey.

scenes.title: Keep the pieces
scenes.alt: Milla arranges paper and fabric model pieces in a tray while Dot compares them with a matching picture card.
scenes.question: Did we keep track of every part?
scenes.learningUse: Discuss material recovery, method limitations and missing pieces without a numerical claim.

scenes.title: A small tidy-up
scenes.alt: Pip returns large paper offcuts to a basket while Dot puts an unlettered notebook on a low classroom shelf.
scenes.question: What can we use again?
scenes.learningUse: Make resetting the workspace a shared responsibility without unsupported recycling claims.

scenes.title: Window weather watchers
scenes.alt: Pip points toward a cloudy window view as Milla holds a blank observation card and Dot records in a notebook.
scenes.question: What is happening now?
scenes.learningUse: Separate observed weather, a forecast and a model; record time and source in native text.

scenes.title: The wind ribbon
scenes.alt: Milla observes a short ribbon on a low stable stand, with a gentle bend suggesting a light breeze.
scenes.question: What does this ribbon tell us, and what does it not?
scenes.learningUse: Introduce a qualitative wind indicator; avoid calling it a calibrated anemometer.

scenes.title: A tiny water test
scenes.alt: Pip transfers a small amount of water from a scoop into a shallow tray while Dot holds a cloth at its edge.
scenes.question: Where does the water go?
scenes.learningUse: Support a teacher-supervised absorption model and noticing where water is transferred.

scenes.title: A plan for a rainy day
scenes.alt: Milla, Dot and two miniature learners compare indoor-table and outdoor-path picture cards beside a closed umbrella on a rainy day.
scenes.question: Which plan fits today?
scenes.learningUse: Choose accessible indoor alternatives based on teacher checks and conditions.

scenes.title: After the rain
scenes.alt: Pip and Milla observe reflections in a shallow puddle from its dry edge, with a closed umbrella in a stand.
scenes.question: What changed, and what stayed the same?
scenes.learningUse: Invite before-and-after comparison without claiming actual Glenoria weather or water quality.

scenes.title: The looking circle
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla and Dot observe a separate miniature garden-patch model with insect picture cards and leaves.
scenes.question: What connections might we investigate?
scenes.learningUse: Introduce possible relationships as questions rather than a surveyed food web.

scenes.title: Leave a little space
scenes.alt: Milla and Dot observe a small insect model resting on a separate leaf, with a closed notebook nearby.
scenes.question: How can we look without disturbing?
scenes.learningUse: Discuss respectful observation and teacher-selected picture alternatives.

scenes.title: The connection string
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla, Dot and two learners connect blank cards with short pieces of string on a low board.
scenes.question: What is our evidence for this connection?
scenes.learningUse: Build and critique a relationship model; strings represent hypotheses until supported.

scenes.title: Two possible stories
scenes.alt: Pip and Dot compare two leaf-picture cards and a blank card while three learners watch.
scenes.question: Could there be another explanation?
scenes.learningUse: Separate observation from causal explanation; seek evidence for alternatives.

scenes.title: The gentle observer
scenes.alt: Dot sketches a leaf in a notebook resting on a cushion beside a leaf prop and a miniature garden-view frame.
scenes.question: Can I watch a little longer?
scenes.learningUse: Provide a calm solo noticing moment; no obligation to touch a living thing.

scenes.title: The hand-to-hand story
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla and Dot pass a plain parcel while four learners follow plant, making and basket picture cards.
scenes.question: Whose work could be part of this story?
scenes.learningUse: Map a fictional plant-product chain and distinguish verified provenance from a model.

scenes.title: Ask the maker
scenes.alt: Milla listens to two learners beside a low table of paper and fabric samples; one learner offers a blank question card.
scenes.question: What would help us check where it came from?
scenes.learningUse: Practise respectful evidence questions; useful for fictional maker interviews.

scenes.title: The paper relay
scenes.alt: Pip, Dot and a learner follow three separate trays containing dry paper strips, a plain sheet and a folded paper boat.
scenes.question: Which step does our model show?
scenes.learningUse: Support Stage 3 paper-process explanation and broader material-to-product sequencing.

scenes.title: The claim check
scenes.alt: Pip holds a blank product tag while Milla opens an evidence folder to blank ivory pages.
scenes.question: What evidence would support that claim?
scenes.learningUse: Distinguish a label/claim from evidence; no invented origin or environmental credential.

scenes.title: A place at the table
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla, Dot and three learners share idea cards around an accessible round table, including a learner using a wheelchair and a learner wearing a head covering.
scenes.question: Has everyone had a way to contribute?
scenes.learningUse: Model reciprocal community planning and multiple ways to take part.

scenes.title: A big idea in a little model
scenes.alt: Pip holds a wall piece, Milla steadies a base and Dot studies a blank plan beside a small open card model.
scenes.question: What problem are we trying to solve?
scenes.learningUse: Frame a classroom design problem; model is not a Glenolia building or approved plan.

scenes.title: The reach test
scenes.alt: Milla and two learners test a low adjustable picture stand, including a learner using a wheelchair.
scenes.question: Can more people use it comfortably?
scenes.learningUse: Invite access considerations without claiming standards compliance from an illustration.

scenes.title: A balancing act
scenes.alt: Pip and Dot test a small cardboard bridge with a single wooden token across two low blocks.
scenes.question: What will we keep the same when we test?
scenes.learningUse: Model a teacher-controlled test and consistent conditions; not a real load-rating exercise.

scenes.title: Try a different shape
scenes.alt: Pip and Milla exchange blank feedback cards beside two simple card prototypes.
scenes.question: What would we change, and why?
scenes.learningUse: Use specific feedback and criteria; change a design rather than judging a learner.

scenes.title: Put the tools to bed
scenes.alt: Milla packs large card shapes into a shallow box while Dot puts a pencil in a holder beside a small card model.
scenes.question: What is ready for next time?
scenes.learningUse: Normalise stopping, resetting and planning the next manageable step.

scenes.title: The evidence picnic
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla and Dot arrange botanical sketches, colour cards and an open notebook on a low mat.
scenes.question: What can our records show?
scenes.learningUse: Revisit a portfolio using dated/source-labelled native records; the scene is illustrative.

scenes.title: A thought changes
scenes.alt: Pip holds a fresh blank idea card and a pencil while an earlier card remains nearby.
scenes.question: What do I think now, and what changed my mind?
scenes.learningUse: Make revision visible and keep earlier thinking as useful evidence.

scenes.title: Tell me how you know
scenes.alt: Milla and Dot listen as a learner points to a blank presentation board; Dot holds a question card.
scenes.question: Which part supports your explanation?
scenes.learningUse: Rehearse evidence-based explanation with pointing, oral or written response options.

scenes.title: A kind second look
scenes.alt: Pip and Milla offer each other blank feedback cards across a low table beside two simple botanical drawings.
scenes.question: What is one useful next step?
scenes.learningUse: Teach specific feedback and moderation without public rankings.

scenes.title: See you next season
scenes.alt: Pip, Milla, Dot and two learners share a friendly wave around a closed learning folder and a blank card.
scenes.question: Which question shall we carry forward?
scenes.learningUse: Close a unit or year with a next inquiry; no promise of a farm opening or event.

classroomTools.title: Four ways to learn
classroomTools.description: Observe, ask, try and reflect: four calm illustrated posters with useful learner questions.
classroomTools.printNote: Print at A3 for a wall display or reduce to A4. These posters contain no measurement scale.

classroomTools.title: Care for the garden, care for each other
classroomTools.description: Two posters about safe participation and gentle care for living things.
classroomTools.printNote: Print at A3 or reduce to A4. Use with the school's own safety procedures.

classroomTools.title: Our 2027 classroom calendar
classroomTools.description: Twelve Monday-first monthly grids, with space for a class question and observation plans. No school dates or farm events are prefilled.
classroomTools.printNote: A4 landscape, single-sided. Enlarge to A3 for more writing room.

classroomTools.title: A week of little discoveries
classroomTools.description: An undated seven-day planner and a reusable inquiry planning sheet.
classroomTools.printNote: Print or laminate an unmarked copy for repeated teacher-led use.

classroomTools.title: Growing curiosity: full-size height banner
classroomTools.description: A native 0-180 cm scale for voluntary classroom measurement activities, with an exact 100 mm calibration bar.
classroomTools.printNote: Specialist large-format print at actual size (100%). Never fit to page. Use the A4 tiled edition for a home or school printer.

classroomTools.title: Growing curiosity: A4 height chart kit
classroomTools.description: Assembly instructions and eight overlapping A4 tiles for the same accurate 0-180 cm banner.
classroomTools.printNote: Actual size (100%), single-sided. Check the 100 mm bar with a ruler before assembly. Match the A-G crosses within the 20 mm overlaps and place the 0 cm line at floor level.

classroomTools.title: Our shared learning quest
classroomTools.description: A reusable group challenge board and a smaller group tracker. Celebrate evidence, helpful actions and next steps together.
classroomTools.printNote: Choose the page size shown for each page. Use group codes and shared goals, not public individual rankings.

classroomTools.title: Six ways to help a learning crew
classroomTools.description: Cut-out cards for observer, recorder, questioner, materials keeper, encourager and checker. Roles can be shared, changed or adapted.
classroomTools.printNote: Print single-sided. An adult cuts along the light guides. Swap roles without making a role a fixed label for a learner.

classroomTools.title: Weather watchers
classroomTools.description: A five-observation record and a page for noticing patterns, methods and unanswered questions.
classroomTools.printNote: Blank records for teacher-approved observations. Keep instrument readings separate from app estimates.

classroomTools.title: Pip's plant observation journal
classroomTools.description: Repeatable plant observations, sketches and an evidence-based comparison. Record the same plant and method each time.
classroomTools.printNote: Use a safe teacher-selected plant. Leave unobserved values blank; the artwork is not real plant data.
classroomTools.use: Classroom, school grounds, optional home observation

classroomTools.title: Little reflections, useful next steps
classroomTools.description: Eight reusable response cards for noticing, wondering, trying, evidence, teamwork and changing an idea.
classroomTools.printNote: Print single-sided and cut into four cards per page. Responses can be spoken, drawn, written or supported.
classroomTools.use: Classroom, indoor workshop, optional home reflection

classroomTools.title: We make room for every learner
classroomTools.description: A welcoming classroom agreement poster and a blank space for the learning crew's own extra agreement.
classroomTools.printNote: Print at A3 or reduce to A4. Add a group code rather than personal learner details.
